metaDescription: Five countertop dishwashers under $500 with real capacity: Energy Star faucet-fed units, a delay-start model and an 8-program tank washer, ranked by fit.
expertTake: The Comfee Energy Star unit is the best overall under $500 because six settings and faucet feed are what a bigger budget should buy. The Euhomy eight-program tank washer is the value pick for renters. Skip the category entirely if you regularly cook for a crowd or wash large roasting pans.
introParagraphs: A five hundred dollar ceiling does not buy a fancier mini. It buys the ability to skip the compromises of the smallest machines: a faucet-fed chamber that holds a proper load, a certified efficiency rating and controls that behave like a real dishwasher.

Listing prices shift from week to week, and the cap reflects prices when this guide was updated. The lineup below leans on larger, six-setting machines, with one tank-fed unit included for kitchens that cannot accept a hose.

products.name: Comfee Energy Star Countertop Dishwasher, 6 Settings, 8 Programs
products.description:
When the budget is high, the logical purchase is the machine that holds the most. This Comfee lists six place settings and a piece count near 70, which gets close to a household's dinner for two with leftovers. A faucet hose supplies water, so wash time is set by the program rather than by tank volume.

Eight programs include speed and baby care options, and the Energy Star certification gives it a verified efficiency claim that most tank-fed minis lack. Dimensions are the cost: 19.7 inches deep and 21.7 inches wide, and the faucet adaptor is not always included or compatible. If you live with a pull-out spout, confirm the thread before you order, because forcing the fit leads to leaks.

For ownership, the routine is similar to a built-in machine on a smaller scale. Load plates facing the center, keep cups angled and let the filter screen get a quick rinse every few cycles. It is the right pick when you want a countertop machine to feel as normal as possible.
products.bestFor: Households of two to four that want the closest thing to a full-size machine.
pros: Six place settings and about 70 pieces per load
Energy Star certification backs the efficiency claim
Faucet feed removes tank-filling chores
Eight programs cover speed, baby care and regular soil
cons: Large 19.7 by 21.7 inch footprint on the counter
Adaptor compatibility depends on your faucet thread
Cannot be used away from a sink

products.name: SPT SD-2225DWA Energy Star Countertop Dishwasher, Delay Start
products.description:
The SPT SD-2225DWA pairs the same six-setting capacity with a feature the Comfee does not list: delay start. Scheduling a wash to finish overnight or during off-peak hours is the kind of control owners of full-size machines take for granted. It adds an LED display, an Energy Star rating and a stated height of only 17.24 inches, which helps it slide under many wall cabinets.

The maker describes dishware up to 10.25 inches in diameter, which marks the practical plate limit. That is slightly smaller than a large dinner plate, so check your own set. Compared with the Comfee it gives similar capacity with a more office-and-apartment character, but the listing offers little detail on cycle count or hot wash temperature, so read the manual before you plan on baby-bottle sanitizing.

People who run the machine in the evening and want dishes clean by morning will find it a good fit. Maintenance is the standard small-washer list: filter rinse, seal wipe and a monthly hot cycle. Place it on a stable surface with space for the door to swing.
products.bestFor: Office kitchens and apartments that want a scheduled overnight wash.
pros: Delay start lets you schedule washes around your day
Six standard place settings in a compact body
Stated height of 17.24 inches clears most cabinets
Energy Star certification and LED display
cons: Plate limit of 10.25 inches excludes large dinnerware
Listing says little about cycle count or hot wash heat
Needs a faucet connection to operate

products.name: Black+Decker BCD6W Energy Star Countertop Dishwasher
products.description:
The BCD6W is built around approachable controls. An LED display shows the cycle and the remaining time, and a Quick Connect assembly attaches the hose to the faucet without hunting for adaptors. Seven wash cycles give a range from light to heavy, and the Energy Star certification keeps it in the efficient group.

The listing supplies fewer hard numbers than the SPT or the Comfee. There is no capacity or temperature figure in the text we evaluated, so shoppers should confirm those details in the manual. What it offers instead is a familiar brand and a layout that is easy for guests to understand, which matters in shared kitchens and for older relatives.

As a faucet-fed machine it shares the same constraints as the Comfee: a threaded spout, a spot near the sink and a bit of care about hoses. The filter and door seal need the usual attention, and a quarterly look at the connection prevents slow leaks inside the cabinet.
products.bestFor: Shared kitchens where simple controls and a trusted name matter.
pros: LED display shows cycle and time remaining
Quick Connect assembly speeds the faucet hookup
Seven cycles from light to heavy loads
Energy Star certification for efficient operation
cons: Listing gives no capacity or hot-wash temperature
Faucet-only, so it suits renters poorly
Fewer stated details than the SPT or the Comfee

products.name: Euhomy 8-Program Countertop Dishwasher, 5L Tank, 29-Min Wash

specList.label: Water supply
specList.value: 5L tank or hose to a G3/4 in faucet

products.description:
This Euhomy is the pick for kitchens that cannot host a hose. A built-in 5 liter tank means you can set it down anywhere with power, and an included hose lets you switch to a G3/4 inch faucet if you want unattended cycles. Two spray arms give 360 degree coverage, and a 29 minute quick wash handles lightly soiled loads.

Eight programs sit on top of the listing, which is the longest list in this group, and plates are rated up to 10.25 inches with about 30 or more items per load. Compared with the six-setting Comfee, it holds less and has to be refilled, but it fits into a 16.85 by 16.73 inch cube, almost three inches smaller on each side. That makes it the compact choice when the budget is high but counter space is not.

Treat it as a flexible small-household machine. Scrape plates, use the quick wash for cups and light plates and move to a longer program for dried-on food. Empty the tank when the machine will sit, and clean the filter regularly to protect spray pressure.
products.bestFor: Renters who want eight programs without touching the faucet.
pros: Eight programs, the longest list in this group
Tank or faucet hose supply in one body
29 minute quick wash for light loads
Compact 16.85 inch cube footprint
cons: Holds fewer dishes than the six-setting machines
Manual fill when the tank mode is used

products.name: Hamilton Beach HBDW3208 Countertop Portable Dishwasher
products.description:
The Hamilton Beach HBDW3208 is the plain option in this lineup. The listing sticks to three claims: it holds up to six standard place settings, it uses little water and it connects to a kitchen tap. There is no program list or temperature figure in the text, which makes it a machine you should read about in the manual before purchase.

Its value is straightforward. A six-setting chamber matches the Comfee and the SPT on capacity, and a plain control scheme suits people who want fewer buttons. It lacks the Energy Star listing, the delay start of the SPT and the display of the Black+Decker, so it competes on simplicity rather than features.

Ownership follows the faucet-fed pattern: attach the hose, load, run and disconnect, and keep the filter clean. It makes sense for apartment dwellers who already know a counter washer fits their life and just want a conventional white box that does the job.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want six settings and a faucet connection without extra features.
pros: Six standard place settings from a familiar appliance name
Described as a low water consumption design
Connects to the kitchen tap like a full-size washer
Plain layout with few controls to learn
cons: No delay start, display or Energy Star claim in the listing
Listing gives no program list or wash temperature
Faucet-only supply rules out tank use

buyingCriteria.explanation: At this budget the faucet-fed units get a real advantage: they never run out of water mid-cycle, and their chambers are usually larger. The Comfee, SPT, Black+Decker and Hamilton Beach all use a hose, while the Euhomy uses a 5 liter tank or a G3/4 inch hose. The Euhomy is the choice for kitchens that cannot accept a hose. Check your faucet thread first. Unscrew the aerator and look for external threads on the spout. A smooth spout or a pull-out sprayer usually means the adaptor will not seat, and a hose forced onto the wrong fitting is the most common source of countertop dishwasher leaks.

Six standard place settings is the top of the countertop class. The Comfee, SPT and Hamilton Beach all claim it, while the Euhomy counts 30 plus items. The SPT limits dishware to 10.25 inches in diameter, and the Euhomy also rates plates to 10.25 inches. Compare your own plates with that limit before you buy. Modern dinner plates often run 10.5 to 11 inches, which means a 10.25 inch rack limit can exclude the plates you actually own. Salad plates and bowls fit easily, so owners with large plates sometimes end up washing only part of the set in the machine.

Energy Star is an independent label, not a marketing slogan. The Comfee, SPT and Black+Decker carry it, while the Hamilton Beach and Euhomy listings do not mention it. Countertop washers use little water anyway, so the label matters mostly as a quality signal. It also helps when you compare similar machines. A certified unit has passed a standard test load for water and power, which a seller's own slogan has not. If two machines look equal on paper, the certified one is the safer bet for long-term running costs and for resale.

A larger budget should buy better controls. The SPT adds delay start and an LED display, and the Black+Decker offers an LED display for cycle and time. Delay start lets you run the machine overnight, which cuts noise and fits your schedule. Simple dial machines still work, but they ask you to be present. Running overnight also keeps heat and steam out of the kitchen during the evening, and it avoids the noise of a pump while you watch television or sleep in a studio apartment.

Six-setting units are bigger. The Comfee measures 19.7 by 21.7 inches, and the SPT is described at 17.24 inches tall. The Euhomy cube is 16.85 by 16.73 inches. Measure under cabinets and leave room for the door, because a washer you cannot open fully is a poor purchase. Also leave a few inches behind the unit for the hose bend and for steam, and keep the power cord away from the sink. A machine pushed tight against a backsplash tends to kink its hose.

A short program helps when you want clean cups by dinner. The Euhomy lists a 29 minute quick wash, which only suits lightly soiled items. Heavier loads need the longer programs. Do not use a quick cycle for dried-on food, because short cycles use less heat and less time. A common mistake is to choose the quick program every night to save electricity, then rewash the plates that still carry film. Use it for cups, glasses and plates rinsed at the sink, and keep the standard program for everything else.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity versus footprint
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated place settings against dimensions, looking at the Comfee's 19.7 by 21.7 inches for six settings versus the Euhomy's 16.85 inch cube. A larger body must deliver real capacity. We favored machines where the extra space shows up as dishes.

howWeEvaluated.title: Water supply options
howWeEvaluated.description: We counted how each machine takes water. Four of the five use a faucet hose, while the Euhomy adds a tank. Flexibility earned credit for renters, and hands-off feed earned credit for busy households.

howWeEvaluated.title: Efficiency and certification
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked which listings mention Energy Star and which do not. The Comfee, SPT and Black+Decker earned the most credit. Listings with no certification claim were not penalized heavily, because the water use of the whole category is low.

howWeEvaluated.title: Controls and scheduling
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at displays and scheduling features, with the SPT's delay start and the Black+Decker's LED display as benchmarks. A higher budget should buy better usability.

howWeEvaluated.title: Budget positioning
howWeEvaluated.description: We kept every pick at or below the cap on live listing price and, based on the spec sheet and owner feedback patterns, asked what the extra money buys over a lower cap. The answer is capacity, certification and scheduling.

maintenance.why: Debris blocks the screen and weakens spray. A blocked filter explains most weak-wash complaints.
Residue collects in the gasket and spreads odor. A quick wipe protects the seal.
A worn washer or loose connection leaks into the cabinet. Dry the fitting and look for damp spots.
Grease and scale build quietly. Use dishwasher cleaner, never hand soap.
Euhomy only. Standing water grows odor in a closed chamber.

faq.q: What does a $500 cap buy that a lower cap does not?
faq.a: Mostly capacity and certification. Six place settings, Energy Star labels and delay start show up in this band, while cheaper tank minis hold four settings or fewer.

faq.q: Which one works without a faucet?
faq.a: The Euhomy eight-program machine, which has a 5 liter tank. The other four rely on a faucet hose, so they suit homeowners and permanent kitchens better than rentals.

faq.q: Is delay start worth paying for?
faq.a: If you run the machine at night, yes. It lets you load after dinner and wake up to clean dishes, and it moves noise out of waking hours.
Check the diameter limit. The SPT and Euhomy quote 10.25 inches, so a 11 inch dinner plate may not fit. Measure before ordering.
With clean filters and dry seals, small pumps and heaters last for years. Hard-water scale and neglected screens are the usual causes of early trouble.

faq.q: Can I put pots and pans in?
faq.a: Small saucepans might fit, but large pots and baking sheets will not. Keep a sink handy for those items and use the machine for plates, cups and cutlery.
